newsitem.title: FRANCE: Notat wins vote to head French unemployment fund.
newsitem.headline: Notat wins vote to head French unemployment fund.

text.p: Nicole Notat, leader of the CFDT labour union, was elected on Tuesday head of France's unemployment benefit fund UNEDIC, beating a virulent critic of the centre-right government for the job.
Notat won 38 out of 50 votes. Her nearest rival, Marc Blondel, head of the Force Ouvriere, collected five votes. There were several spoiled ballots.
Notat's election was virtually a foregone conclusion after she received backing from the national employers' federation, CNPF, on Monday.
Notat's union is pro-Socialist but backs the controversial welfare reforms set in motion by Prime Minister Alain Juppe last year.
The victory gives Notat the job of managing the strategically important unemployment fund along with the employers and is a setback for Blondel.

Last July, the CFDT union ousted him from another strategic role at the head of the public health insurance fund, the Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie, a post of power and patronage the FO had held for 30 years.
Notat has signalled she does not fully share the goals of employers, campaigning for a cut in the payroll contributions which are the lifeblood of the UNEDIC unemployment fund.
She also said in a newspaper interview on Monday that the unemployed should be the first to benefit from any surplus in the fund.
The UNEDIC fund expects to post a 1996 surplus of 12 billion francs after running heavily into debt in the early 1990s.

To qualify for European monetary union, the government is planning to use the surplus in the unemployment fund as an off-budget revenue to get its public deficit below three percent of gross domestic product in 1997.
